scenario: Debating the pros and cons of remote work
frequency_note: words ranked ~1500–3000 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used for quantities or levels.
Opposite of 늘다.
Common in work contexts.
Also used as verb 집중하다.
Describes something that makes life easier.
Used in expressions like 불편을 느끼다 (to feel discomfort).

vocabulary.translation: to follow, to depend on, to accompany
vocabulary.note: With 에 따르면 = according to.
Used with -는 경우에 = in case of.
Connects contrasts in formal discourse.
Indicates an unexpected consequence.
Used to add information.
Common with 계획하다 (to plan) or 준비하다 (to prepare).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 요즘 재택근무를 하면서 업무 효율이 늘었다고 느끼는 사람들이 많아요.
dialogue.translation: These days, many people feel that work efficiency has increased with remote work.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그래요? 저는 오히려 집중이 줄었어요. 집에는 방해 요소가 너무 많아요.
dialogue.translation: Really? I, on the contrary, have lost concentration. There are too many distractions at home.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그런 경우도 있지만, 저는 출퇴근 시간이 없어서 훨씬 편해요.
dialogue.translation: That may be the case, but I feel much more comfortable because I don't have to commute.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 하지만 재택근무는 동료들과의 소통이 불편할 뿐만 아니라, 업무와 생활의 경계가 없어져요.
dialogue.translation: But remote work not only makes communication with colleagues inconvenient, but also blurs the boundary between work and life.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아요. 하지만 반면에, 재택근무를 하면 시간을 미리 계획해서 더 효율적으로 쓸 수 있어요.
dialogue.translation: That's right. But on the other hand, with remote work, you can plan your time in advance and use it more efficiently.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그건 인정해요. 다만, 모든 직업에 재택근무가 맞는 건 아니에요. 상황에 따라 달라요.
dialogue.translation: I admit that. However, remote work is not suitable for all jobs. It depends on the situation.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 물론이죠. 그래도 재택근무의 장점을 활용하면 회사와 직원 모두에게 좋은 결과가 따를 거예요.
dialogue.translation: Of course. Still, if we take advantage of the benefits of remote work, good results will follow for both the company and employees.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 좋은 의견이에요. 결국 중요한 건 균형을 찾는 거라고 생각해요.
dialogue.translation: Good opinion. In the end, I think what's important is finding a balance.

scenario: Discussing a complex ethical dilemma
frequency_note: words ranked ~1500–3000 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used to describe a person or action that is honest.
Refers to the ability to decide or evaluate.

vocabulary.translation: to decide, to make a decision
vocabulary.note: Common verb for 'to decide'.
Refers to the internal sense of right and wrong.
Used to compare things that resemble each other.
Can refer to physical weight or the importance of something.

vocabulary.translation: to judge, to evaluate, to form a judgment
vocabulary.note: Verbal variant of '판단'.
Used to talk about ethical or moral values.
Describes something with many elements or difficult to understand.
Used in contexts of making decisions.
Refers to the obligation to answer for one's actions.
Used to indicate that something is not ambiguous.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 이 상황은 정말 복잡한 윤리적 딜레마인 것 같아. 네 판단은 어때?
dialogue.translation: This situation seems like a really complex ethical dilemma. What's your judgment?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 솔직히, 내 양심에 따르면 정직한 선택을 해야 해. 하지만 그게 항상 옳은 결과를 가져오는 건 아니잖아.
dialogue.translation: Honestly, according to my conscience, I should make the honest choice. But that doesn't always bring the right result, right?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 그런데 책임을 생각하면, 다른 사람에게 미치는 영향도 무시할 수 없어. 그 무게를 어떻게 판단해야 할까?
dialogue.translation: Right. But thinking about responsibility, you can't ignore the impact on others. How should we judge that weight?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 내 생각에는, 결정하기 전에 서로 다른 가치들 사이에서 우선순위를 정하는 게 중요해. 모든 가치가 비슷해 보이지만, 실제로는 달라.
dialogue.translation: In my opinion, before deciding, it's important to set priorities among different values. All values seem similar, but in reality they are different.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그렇지. 하지만 어떤 경우에는 그 가치들이 너무 상충해서 분명한 답이 없을 때도 있어. 그럴 때 어떻게 해야 한다고 생각해?
dialogue.translation: Yes, that's right. But sometimes the values conflict so much that there's no clear answer. What do you think should be done in that case?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그럴 땐 장기적인 결과를 생각해 봐야 해. 단기적인 선택이 옳아 보여도, 나중에 후회할 수도 있으니까.
dialogue.translation: In those cases, you should think about the long-term consequences. Even if a short-term choice seems right, you might regret it later.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 좋은 지적이야. 하지만 모든 사람이 같은 기준으로 판단하는 건 아니잖아. 그래서 더 복잡해지는 거지.
dialogue.translation: Good point. But not everyone judges by the same standards. That's why it becomes more complicated.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 맞아, 결국은 자신의 양심과 책임을 잘 저울질해서 결정해야 해. 그게 최선의 방법이야.
dialogue.translation: Right, in the end you have to decide by carefully weighing your conscience and responsibility. That's the best way.

key_phrases.translation: to follow one's conscience (act according to conscience)
to evaluate the weight (importance) of something

scenario: Analyzing the impact of social media on society
frequency_note: words ranked ~1500–3000 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Common noun for 'influence' or 'effect'.
Noun for 'society'.
Person who uses something, common in technology contexts.
Used for the spread of information or ideas.
Point of view or perspective.
Act of expressing ideas or feelings.
State of being free.
Action of setting limits.
Adverb indicating contrast or unexpected result.
Logical connector of cause and effect.
Action of judging or pointing out flaws.
Exchange of opinions in a structured manner.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 요즘 소셜 미디어가 사회에 미치는 영향이 정말 크잖아.
dialogue.translation: These days, the impact that social media has on society is really big, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 맞아. 특히 사용자들이 정보의 확산 속도가 너무 빨라서 문제야.
dialogue.translation: Right. Especially, the problem is that the speed of information spread among users is too fast.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그런데 의견을 자유롭게 표현할 수 있다는 점은 좋은 것 같아.
dialogue.translation: But I think the fact that we can freely express opinions is a good thing.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그렇지만 너무 자유로우면 오히려 문제가 생길 수 있어. 예를 들어, 악성 댓글이나 허위 정보가 퍼지잖아.
dialogue.translation: However, if there is too much freedom, problems can arise on the contrary. For example, malicious comments or false information spread.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아, 그래서 어떤 제한이 필요하다고 생각해. 하지만 지나친 제한은 표현의 자유를 침해할 수 있어.
dialogue.translation: Right, so I think some restriction is necessary. But excessive restriction can infringe on freedom of expression.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 따라서 우리는 균형을 찾아야 해. 그리고 비판을 할 때도 서로 존중하는 토론 문화가 중요해.
dialogue.translation: Therefore, we need to find a balance. And also when criticizing, a culture of debate with mutual respect is important.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 동의해. 결국 소셜 미디어의 영향은 우리가 어떻게 사용하느냐에 달려 있으니까.
dialogue.translation: I agree. After all, the impact of social media depends on how we use it.

scenario: Presenting a business proposal
frequency_note: words ranked ~1500–3000 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Common verb for 'to propose' in formal and everyday contexts.
Used to refer to documents, data, or presentation material.
Common in business and planning contexts.
Also means 'mayor', but in business it is 'market'.
Frequent in economic and business contexts.
Used to talk about projections or estimates.
Adjective describing a positive and energetic attitude.
Used for 'preparing' resources, funds, plans, etc.
Key word in planning contexts.
Refers to economic benefit or advantage.
Used with verbs like '하다' or '되다' to mean 'to secure' something.
Specific for money intended for a purpose.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 안녕하세요, 오늘 저희가 새 프로젝트를 제안하려고 합니다.
dialogue.translation: Hello, today we are going to propose a new project.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 먼저 준비하신 자료를 보여 주시겠어요?
dialogue.translation: Yes, could you show us the materials you have prepared first?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 물론입니다. 저희의 주된 목표는 신흥 시장에서의 성장을 이루는 것입니다.
dialogue.translation: Of course. Our main goal is to achieve growth in the emerging market.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 성장 가능성에 대한 예상 수치가 있습니까?
dialogue.translation: Do you have forecast figures for the growth potential?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 네, 저희는 적극적인 마케팅으로 매출을 늘릴 계획입니다.
dialogue.translation: Yes, we plan to increase sales with active marketing.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그렇다면 초기 자금은 어떻게 마련하실 건가요?
dialogue.translation: Then, how do you plan to secure the initial capital?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 투자자들로부터 자금을 확보하고, 장기적인 이익을 약속드릴 수 있습니다.
dialogue.translation: We can secure funds from investors and promise long-term profits.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 좋습니다. 그 계획에 대해 더 자세히 논의해 봅시다.
dialogue.translation: Good. Let's discuss that plan in more detail.

scenario: Discussing mental health and wellbeing openly
frequency_note: words ranked ~1500–3000 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used to refer to mental/emotional state in wellbeing contexts.
Can combine with '정신적' for mental health.
Adjective derived from 정신 (spirit/mind).
Loanword from English, very common.
Used to talk about emotions in general.
Related to 표현 (expression), already seen, but here as a verb.
Common in therapy or counseling contexts.
Can refer to medical or psychological treatment.
Used with 하다 (필요하다) or in structures like 필요가 있다.
Adverb that emphasizes reciprocity.
More formal than 말하기; used for meaningful conversations.
Compound of 자존 (self-esteem) and 감 (feeling).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 요즘 마음이 많이 힘들어요. 스트레스가 너무 커서 자존감이 떨어진 것 같아요.
dialogue.translation: Lately I feel very bad emotionally. The stress is so great that I feel my self-esteem has dropped.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 정신적 건강은 정말 중요하죠. 감정을 솔직하게 표현하는 게 도움이 돼요.
dialogue.translation: Mental health is really important, right? Expressing your emotions honestly helps.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아요. 그런데 주변 사람들에게 부담을 주지 않을까 걱정돼요.
dialogue.translation: That's right. But I worry about being a burden to those around me.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 서로 대화하는 게 중요해요. 상담을 받는 것도 좋은 방법이에요.
dialogue.translation: It's important to talk to each other. Getting counseling is also a good option.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 상담을 받아 본 적이 없어서 조금 낯설어요. 치료가 꼭 필요한 걸까요?
dialogue.translation: I've never had counseling before, so it feels a bit unfamiliar. Is treatment really necessary?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 필요는 사람마다 달라요. 하지만 전문가의 도움을 받으면 훨씬 수월해질 수 있어요.
dialogue.translation: The need varies from person to person. But with professional help, it can become much easier.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그렇군요. 먼저 가까운 사람들과 대화를 나눠 보려고요. 그리고 필요하면 상담을 알아볼게요.
dialogue.translation: I see. First, I'll try talking with close people. And if necessary, I'll look into counseling.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 좋은 생각이에요. 서로의 감정을 존중하고 잘 표현하면 자존감도 회복될 거예요.
dialogue.translation: Good idea. If you respect and express each other's feelings well, your self-esteem will recover.

scenario: Talking about urban vs rural living
frequency_note: words ranked ~1500–3000 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used as a predicative verb or adjective in health contexts.
Refers to both natural and social environment.
E.g., hospital facilities, educational facilities.
Common for traveling or changing location.
In the context of air quality.
Used for convenience of services or transportation.
Opposite of noisy.
Refers to physical or living space.
Formal, common in texts and conversations.
Used with '에' to indicate access to something.
Indicates lack or deficiency.
Adversative connector, more formal than '하지만'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 도시에 살면 모든 시설에 접근하기가 정말 편리해.
dialogue.translation: Living in the city makes it really convenient to access all facilities.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 맞아, 하지만 공기 질이 나쁘고 항상 시끄러워서 건강에 좋지 않은 것 같아.
dialogue.translation: Right, but the air quality is bad and it's always noisy, so it seems like it's not good for your health.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그러나 시골은 조용하고 공간이 넓어서 마음이 편안해져.
dialogue.translation: However, in the countryside it's quiet and there's plenty of space, so you feel at peace.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그런데 시골에는 병원이나 학교 같은 시설이 부족해서 이동하는 데 시간이 많이 걸려.
dialogue.translation: But in the countryside, facilities like hospitals or schools are lacking, so it takes a lot of time to get around.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아, 하지만 자연환경이 좋아서 스트레스가 줄어들고 더 건강하게 살 수 있어.
dialogue.translation: Right, but the natural environment is good, so stress decreases and you can live healthier.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 도시는 다양한 문화 시설과 일자리를 제공하니까 그 점이 큰 장점이지.
dialogue.translation: The city provides various cultural facilities and jobs, so that's a big advantage.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 하지만 생활비가 너무 높아서 부담이 되고, 반면 시골은 비용이 적게 들어.
dialogue.translation: But the cost of living is too high and it's a burden, whereas in the countryside the costs are lower.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그러니까 결국 각자 우선순위에 따라 선택하는 게 중요해. 나는 조용한 환경을 더 원해.
dialogue.translation: So in the end, it's important to choose according to each person's priorities. I prefer a quiet environment.

key_phrases.translation: it takes time to get around
the cost of living is a burden

scenario: Negotiating a salary or contract term
frequency_note: words ranked ~1500–3000 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used in negotiation contexts to refer to terms or conditions.
Common verb for negotiating in any field.
Formal term for regular payment for work.
Frequent in '급여 인상' (salary increase).
Can sound strong; in negotiation it is used politely.
Used to say that a proposed condition is accepted.
Used to make concessions or trade-offs in negotiation.
Applies to conditions, schedules, attitudes.

vocabulary.translation: to present, to propose (an offer or condition)
vocabulary.note: In negotiation, used to present a concrete proposal.
Used to talk about modifying figures or conditions.
Important in negotiation: to look for alternative solutions.

vocabulary.translation: to reach an agreement, to agree
vocabulary.note: Final point of a successful negotiation.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 안녕하세요, 저는 이번에 제시된 계약 조건에 대해 이야기하고 싶습니다.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I would like to talk about the contract conditions that have been presented.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 물론입니다. 어떤 부분을 조정하고 싶으신지 말씀해 주세요.
dialogue.translation: Of course. Please tell me which part you would like to adjust.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 우선 급여 인상이 필요하다고 생각합니다. 제 경력에 비해 현재 제안은 좀 낮아요.
dialogue.translation: First, I think a salary increase is necessary. Compared to my experience, the current offer is a bit low.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 이해합니다. 하지만 예산이 넉넉하지 않아서 인상분을 수용하기 어렵습니다.
dialogue.translation: I understand. But the budget is not very ample, so it is difficult to accept the increase.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그러면 급여 대신에 재택근무를 더 허용해 주시겠어요? 저는 시간적으로 유연한 근무 조건이 중요합니다.
dialogue.translation: Then, could you allow more remote work instead of the salary increase? For me, flexible working conditions in terms of time are important.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그것은 좋은 대안이네요. 주 2회 재택근무를 제시해 볼 수 있습니다.
dialogue.translation: That is a good alternative. We can offer two days of remote work per week.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 감사합니다. 그러면 급여 인상은 다음 해에 다시 요구할 수 있을까요?
dialogue.translation: Thank you. Then, can I request a salary increase again next year?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 그렇게 합의할 수 있습니다. 계약서에 명시하겠습니다.
dialogue.translation: Yes, we can agree on that. We will specify it in the contract.

scenario: Debating environmental policy with a peer
frequency_note: words ranked ~1500–3000 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.translation: to assert, to maintain, to argue
to follow, to comply with (a rule); to depend on

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 새로운 환경 정책이 실제로 효과가 있을까?
dialogue.translation: Will the new environmental policy actually have an effect?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 글쎄, 나는 반대야. 비용이 너무 많이 들고, 거의 효과를 못 볼 거야.
dialogue.translation: Well, I'm against it. It costs too much and will have almost no effect.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 하지만 탄소 배출을 줄이려면 어느 정도 비용이 드는 게 당연하지.
dialogue.translation: But to reduce carbon emissions, it's natural that it costs something.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그런데 주장하는 근거가 뭐야? 실제로 배출량이 증가한 경우도 있잖아.
dialogue.translation: But what's the basis for your claim? There are cases where emissions have actually increased.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 연구를 보면, 정책을 잘 따르는 지역에서는 배출량이 줄었어.
dialogue.translation: According to research, in regions that follow the policy well, emissions have decreased.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 좋아, 그렇지만 모든 기업이 정책을 따르는 건 아니야. 비용 문제 때문에.
dialogue.translation: Okay, but not all companies follow the policy, because of the cost issue.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그래도 장기적으로 보면 효과가 클 거야. 지금 비용 때문에 반대하면 안 돼.
dialogue.translation: Still, in the long run, the effect will be big. You shouldn't oppose it just because of the current cost.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 음, 네 근거를 보니 조금은 설득되네. 하지만 실제로 적용되는 경우를 더 봐야겠어.
dialogue.translation: Hmm, seeing your reasoning convinces me a bit. But I need to see more cases of actual application.

scenario: Discussing immigration and identity
frequency_note: words ranked ~1500–3000 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used in contexts of identity and society.
Common in discussions about integration.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 이민 온 지 10년이 지났는데, 아직도 내 정체성이 뭔지 헷갈려.
dialogue.translation: It's been 10 years since I immigrated, and I'm still confused about what my identity is.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그래? 나는 한국 사회에 적응하는 게 제일 어려웠어. 특히 문화 차이 때문에 힘들었지.
dialogue.translation: Really? For me, adapting to Korean society was the hardest. Especially, it was tough because of cultural differences.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 하지만 다양한 사람들을 만나면서 내 생각이 조금씩 바뀌었어.
dialogue.translation: Right. But as I met diverse people, my thinking changed little by little.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그 과정을 통해 너는 어떤 걸 느꼈어?
dialogue.translation: Through that process, what did you feel?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 처음에는 두 문화 사이에서 갈등했지만, 결국 두 정체성을 모두 포함하는 게 가능하다는 걸 알았어.
dialogue.translation: At first, I was conflicted between the two cultures, but in the end, I learned that it's possible to include both identities.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그렇구나. 나는 아직도 한국 사람들과 서로 잘 지내는 게 어렵다고 느껴.
dialogue.translation: I see. I still feel that it's difficult to get along well with Korean people and for them to get along with me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 시간이 지나면 괜찮아질 거야. 중요한 건 너 자신을 믿는 거야.
dialogue.translation: It will get better over time. The important thing is to believe in yourself.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 고마워. 너와 대화하면서 나도 더 긍정적으로 생각하게 됐어.
dialogue.translation: Thanks. Talking with you has made me think more positively too.

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.translation: When analyzing this work, I think the first thing to look at is the theme.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그런데 주제를 파악하려면 인물의 행동과 배경을 같이 봐야 해.
dialogue.translation: But to grasp the theme, you need to look at the characters' actions and the background together.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 특히 주인공이 혼자 있는 장면에서 빨간 색이 자주 나오는데, 그게 무슨 의미일까?
dialogue.translation: Right. Especially in scenes where the protagonist is alone, the color red appears often—what could that mean?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 빨간 색은 아마도 욕망이나 위험을 상징하는 것 같아. 반면에 파란 색은 평화를 나타내고.
dialogue.translation: The red probably symbolizes desire or danger. On the other hand, the blue represents peace.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 흥미롭네. 그런데 이 작품의 구성은 좀 특이해. 시간 순서대로 가지 않고 과거와 현재를 비교하면서 진행되잖아.
dialogue.translation: Interesting. But the structure of this work is a bit unusual. It doesn't follow chronological order; instead, it progresses by comparing past and present.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그래서 처음에는 이해하기 어려웠지만, 전체적으로 보면 그 구성이 주제를 강조하는 데 효과적이야.
dialogue.translation: That's why it was hard to understand at first, but overall, that structure is effective in emphasizing the theme.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 동의해. 특히 마지막 장면에서 주인공의 선택이 모든 걸 바꿔 놓는데, 그게 인물의 성장을 보여 주는 것 같아.
dialogue.translation: Agreed. Especially in the final scene, the protagonist's choice changes everything, and that seems to show the character's growth.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그러니까 결국 이 작품은 인간의 선택과 그 결과에 대한 이야기야. 정말 깊은 의미가 있는 것 같아.
dialogue.translation: So, in the end, this work is a story about human choices and their consequences. I think it has a really deep meaning.

scenario: Discussing the gig economy and job insecurity

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 요즘 경제가 불안정해서 많은 사람들이 일자리를 잃을까 봐 불안해요.
dialogue.translation: These days the economy is unstable, and many people are anxious about losing their jobs.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 맞아요. 특히 배달 앱 같은 데서 일하는 사람들은 고용 계약이 없어서 수입이 보장되지 않아요.
dialogue.translation: That's right. Especially those working for delivery apps don't have employment contracts, so their income isn't guaranteed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그리고 그런 일은 대부분 임시라서 장기적으로 미래를 계획하기 어렵죠.
dialogue.translation: And those jobs are mostly temporary, so it's hard to plan for the future in the long term.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 게다가 평균 수입도 낮고, 일이 없을 때는 정말 불안해요.
dialogue.translation: Besides, the average income is low, and when there's no work, you feel really anxious.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 하지만 어떤 사람들은 시간이 자유로워서 좋아하기도 해요.
dialogue.translation: But some people like it because they have free time.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그래도 고용이 불안정하면 미래를 설계할 수 없잖아요.
dialogue.translation: Still, if employment is unstable, you can't plan your future.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아요. 결국엔 안정적인 일자리를 찾는 게 중요해요.
dialogue.translation: That's right. In the end, finding a stable job is important.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그러니까 정부가 계약을 보장해 주고 장기적인 고용 정책을 만들어야 해요.
dialogue.translation: So the government should guarantee contracts and create long-term employment policies.

key_phrases.translation: plan the future in the long term

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 민주주의에서 가장 중요한 건 시민의 참여라고 생각해. 선거에 참여하지 않으면 대표가 우리를 제대로 대표할 수 없잖아.
dialogue.translation: In democracy, the most important thing is citizen participation. If we don't participate in elections, representatives can't represent us properly.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 물론이지. 그러나 현실적으로 보면 많은 사람들이 정치에 관심이 없어서 투표율이 낮아.
dialogue.translation: Of course. However, in reality, many people are not interested in politics, so voter turnout is low.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그건 문제야. 정부가 법을 만들 때 시민의 의견을 반영하려면 모두가 목소리를 내야 해.
dialogue.translation: That's a problem. For the government to reflect citizens' opinions when making laws, everyone must speak up.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 맞아. 그런데 권력이 한쪽에 집중되면 자유나 평등이 위협받을 수 있어. 그래서 제도가 중요해.
dialogue.translation: Right. But if power is concentrated in one side, freedom and equality can be threatened. That's why the system is important.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그래서 정치 체제를 논할 때는 단순히 누가 통치하는지보다 어떻게 권력을 분산할지가 더 중요하다고 봐.
dialogue.translation: So, when discussing political systems, I think it's more important how power is distributed than simply who governs.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 동의해. 그러나 모든 제도가 완벽할 수는 없어. 시민들이 계속해서 참여하고 감시해야 해.
dialogue.translation: Agreed. But no system can be perfect. Citizens must continue to participate and monitor.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 결국 정치의 목적은 국민의 자유와 평등을 보장하는 거잖아. 물론 그 과정에서 갈등도 생기겠지만.
dialogue.translation: Right. After all, the purpose of politics is to guarantee citizens' freedom and equality. Of course, conflicts will arise in that process.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그러니까 우리 모두가 책임감을 가지고 선거에 참여하고, 법과 제도의 변화를 이끌어내야지. 그래야 진정한 민주주의가 가능해.
dialogue.translation: So we all must participate in elections responsibly and lead changes in laws and systems. Only then is true democracy possible.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 좋아요. 그런데 데이터를 처리하는 단계는 어떻게 작동하나요?
dialogue.translation: Okay. But how does the data processing stage work?

scenario: Discussing the ethics of AI

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: AI가 내리는 판단이 항상 정확하다고 볼 수 있을까?
dialogue.translation: Can we say that the judgments made by AI are always accurate?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 사실, AI도 데이터에 영향을 받기 때문에 오류가 있을 수 있어.
dialogue.translation: Actually, since AI is also influenced by data, it can have errors.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그렇다면 AI의 결정에 대한 책임은 누가 져야 한다고 생각해?
dialogue.translation: Then, who do you think should take responsibility for AI's decisions?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 개발자와 사용자 모두가 고려해야 할 문제지. 특히 위험을 최소화하는 게 중요해.
dialogue.translation: It's a problem that both developers and users must consider. Especially, minimizing risks is important.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아, 기술의 발전이 빠를수록 더 많은 보호 장치가 필요해.
dialogue.translation: Right, the faster technology develops, the more protective measures are needed.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그래서 나는 AI 사용에 대한 명확한 규칙을 만드는 데 동의해.
dialogue.translation: That's why I agree to create clear rules about AI usage.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 하지만 너무 많은 규제가 오히려 혁신을 막을 수도 있지 않을까?
dialogue.translation: But, couldn't too much regulation actually hinder innovation?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그건 균형의 문제야. 윤리적인 판단과 기술의 발전을 함께 고려해야 해.
dialogue.translation: That's a matter of balance. We must consider ethical judgment and technological development together.

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.translation: Really? I thought the younger generation these days divides things more fairly.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 물론 변화가 없지는 않지. 하지만 여전히 집안일이나 육아는 주로 여성의 몫이라는 인식이 강해.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 나도 어렸을 때는 아버지가 어머니 대신에 요리를 하시면 이상하게 생각했거든.
dialogue.translation: Right. When I was young, if my father cooked instead of my mother, I thought it was strange.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그런데 요즘은 많은 남성들이 육아에 적극적으로 참여하면서 역할에 대한 기대도 바뀌고 있어.
dialogue.translation: But these days, as many men actively participate in child rearing, expectations about roles are also changing.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 특히 맞벌이 부부가 늘면서 집안일을 나누는 게 당연해졌어.
dialogue.translation: Right. Especially as dual-income couples increase, sharing housework has become natural.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그래도 아직 갈 길이 멀어. 여성의 사회 진출은 증가했지만, 남성의 육아 참여는 여전히 부족하다는 연구 결과도 있어.
dialogue.translation: Still, there's a long way to go. Although women's participation in society has increased, there are also research results showing that men's participation in child rearing is still insufficient.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그 경험을 통해 자신감을 얻은 것 같아. 예전과 비교하면 정말 다르네.
dialogue.translation: It seems you gained confidence through that experience. Compared to before, you're really different.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 결국 그 모든 것이 나의 성장으로 이어졌어. 이제는 어려운 일이 와도 자신 있게 대처해.
dialogue.translation: Right. In the end, all of that led to my growth. Now, even when difficult things come, I handle them confidently.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그동안 너무 힘들었겠다. 하지만 그 경험이 너를 강하게 만든 거지.
dialogue.translation: It must have been really hard during that time. But that experience made you strong.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그래. 만약 그때 떠나지 않았더라면, 지금의 나는 없었을 거야.
dialogue.translation: Yes. If I hadn't left then, the current me wouldn't exist.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 정말 인생이 바뀌는 경험이었구나. 나도 언젠가 그런 기회를 갖고 싶어.
dialogue.translation: It was truly a life-changing experience. I also want to have such an opportunity someday.

In the context of humor, it means something is not serious or heavy.
Opposite of a comfortable atmosphere; humor relieves tension.
With 긴장, it means 'to relieve tension' (긴장을 풀다).
Used to contrast with joking: 진심으로 = sincerely.
Useful verb for talking about conveying a message or emotion.
Frequent in conversations about communication.
In context: 오해가 생기다 = a misunderstanding arises.
Important in communication: understanding the other person.
Adverb to emphasize clarity.
Describes humor that flows naturally.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 요즘 대화할 때 웃음이 중요한 것 같아. 분위기가 확 살아나잖아.
dialogue.translation: Lately I feel that laughter is important when conversing. The atmosphere really comes alive, doesn't it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 맞아. 특히 처음 만난 사람과는 가벼운 농담이 긴장을 풀어 주는 데 효과적이야.
dialogue.translation: Right. Especially with someone you've just met, a light joke is effective in relieving tension.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그런데 진심을 전하려고 할 때 농담이 오해를 생기게 할 수도 있지 않아?
dialogue.translation: But when you want to convey sincerity, can't a joke cause misunderstandings?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그럴 수 있지. 그래서 상대방의 반응을 분명히 살펴야 해.
dialogue.translation: It can be. That's why you need to clearly observe the other person's reaction.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 그리고 너무 억지로 웃기려고 하면 오히려 자연스럽지 않잖아.
dialogue.translation: Right. And if you try too hard to be funny, it's not natural anymore.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그래서 중요한 건 상황과 상대방의 기분을 고려하는 거야. 그러면 웃음이 진짜 소통을 돕는 도구가 돼.
dialogue.translation: So the important thing is to consider the situation and the other person's mood. Then laughter becomes a tool that truly helps communication.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 결국 유머는 진심을 전하는 하나의 방법이 될 수 있구나.
dialogue.translation: Right. In the end, humor can be a way to convey sincerity.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 응, 잘 사용하면 분위기도 좋아지고 긴장도 풀리고, 오해도 줄일 수 있어.
dialogue.translation: Yes, if used well, it improves the atmosphere, relieves tension, and can reduce misunderstandings.

scenario: Presenting a research finding
frequency_note: words ranked ~1500–3000 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Result of a study or experiment.
Can refer to a survey or field research.
Formal verb for presenting results.
Loanword from English 'data'.
Commonly used in academic contexts.
Evidence that supports a claim.
To explain something clearly.
To assert something based on arguments.
Conclusion of a study or presentation.
Reasoning or evidence that supports a conclusion.
Adverb indicating greater depth.
Formal logical connector, frequent in academic texts.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 오늘 조사 결과를 바탕으로 연구 결과를 보고하겠습니다.
dialogue.translation: Today I will report the research findings based on the survey results.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 그런데 어떤 데이터를 사용했는지 자세히 설명해 주시겠어요?
dialogue.translation: Yes, but could you explain in detail what data you used?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 먼저 설문 조사에서 얻은 데이터를 분석했습니다. 그 결과, 응답자의 70%가 새로운 정책을 지지했습니다.
dialogue.translation: First, I analyzed the data obtained from the survey. As a result, 70% of respondents supported the new policy.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 흥미롭네요. 그런데 그 결과를 뒷받침할 충분한 증거가 있나요?
dialogue.translation: Interesting. But is there sufficient evidence to support that result?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 네, 추가 분석에서도 동일한 패턴이 나타났습니다. 그러므로 이 결과는 신뢰할 만합니다.
dialogue.translation: Yes, additional analyses also showed the same pattern. Therefore, these results are reliable.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그렇다면, 어떤 근거로 그런 결론을 주장하시는 건가요?
dialogue.translation: Then, on what basis do you claim that conclusion?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 주장의 근거는 바로 데이터에서 나온 패턴입니다. 그리고 표본이 충분히 컸기 때문에 결론을 일반화할 수 있습니다.
dialogue.translation: The basis of my claim is the pattern observed in the data. And because the sample was large enough, we can generalize the conclusion.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 좋습니다. 마지막으로 그 결과를 요약해서 설명해 주시겠어요?
dialogue.translation: Good. Finally, could you summarize and explain the results?

scenario: Discussing inequality and social mobility
frequency_note: words ranked ~1500–3000 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used in contexts of social stratification (계층 간 이동).
Frequent in discussions about economic inequality.
Used with '소득 격차' (income gap).
Intransitive verb; opposite of '늘어나다'.
Transitive form, related to '줄어들다'.
Common with '~에도 불구하고' (despite...).
Key factor in social mobility.
Can refer to social or family environment.
Opposite of '과거' (past).
It was already on the exclusion list; that's why it was omitted. (I'll include another)
Used to contrast appearance and reality.
Common adversative connector in colloquial register.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 요즘 한국에서 소득 격차가 점점 커지고 있대. 근데 실제로는 계층 간 이동이 쉬워졌다고 하는 사람들도 있어.
dialogue.translation: They say that in Korea the income gap is getting bigger and bigger. But some people say that in reality, mobility between classes has become easier.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그렇지만 통계를 보면 교육 수준이 높아도 소득이 크게 달라지지 않는 경우가 많아. 환경이 중요한 것 같아.
dialogue.translation: But if you look at the statistics, there are many cases where even if the education level is high, income doesn't change much. I think the environment is important.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아. 좋은 환경에서 자란 사람들은 더 좋은 교육을 받을 기회가 많으니까. 그런데 노력해도 안 되는 경우도 있잖아.
dialogue.translation: Right. People who grow up in a good environment have more opportunities to receive a better education. But there are cases where even if you try, it doesn't work out.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그래서 정부가 소득 격차를 줄이려고 여러 정책을 내놓고 있잖아. 하지만 효과가 있는지 아직 모르겠어.
dialogue.translation: That's why the government is implementing various policies to reduce the income gap. But I still don't know if they are effective.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 교육 투자를 늘리면 장기적으로는 격차가 줄어들 거라고 보는 사람들도 많아. 근데 그건 미래의 문제지.
dialogue.translation: Many people think that if investment in education is increased, the gap will decrease in the long run. But that's a problem for the future.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 맞아. 지금 당장은 생활비 때문에 힘든 사람들이 많으니까. 그런데 우리가 할 수 있는 일이 뭐가 있을까?
dialogue.translation: Right. Right now, many people are struggling because of the cost of living. But what can we do?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 적어도 주변 사람들에게 교육의 중요성을 알리고, 기회를 나누는 게 좋겠지. 그렇지만 큰 변화를 기대하기는 어려워.
dialogue.translation: At least it would be good to raise awareness among those around us about the importance of education and share opportunities. But it's hard to expect a big change.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 맞아. 하지만 우리가 노력하면 조금씩 상황이 나아질 거야. 그래도 정부의 역할이 제일 중요하다고 생각해.
dialogue.translation: Right. But if we make an effort, the situation will gradually improve. Still, I think the government's role is the most important.

key_phrases.translation: cases where even if you try, it doesn't work out

scenario: Talking about leadership styles
frequency_note: words ranked ~1500–3000 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used to refer to a leader in general, not only political.
Common in work or management contexts.
Loanword from English, very used in work environments.
Used with -기로 결정하다 or -을/ㄹ 결정하다.
Frequent in discussions and meetings.
Transitive verb; used with a direct object.
Often in phrases like 책임을 지다 (to take responsibility).
Used to describe communication or rules.
Common in interpersonal or work relationship contexts.
Used with problema, 갈등, etc.
Indicates contrast or unexpected result.
Connector of cause and effect.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 우리 팀의 새 지도자는 결정을 잘 내리는데, 항상 혼자 결정해요.
dialogue.translation: The new leader of our team makes good decisions, but he always decides alone.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그런 방식은 팀원들의 의견을 존중하지 않는다고 느낄 수 있어요.
dialogue.translation: That style can make team members feel that their opinions are not respected.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아요. 그래서 요즘 갈등이 좀 생겼어요.
dialogue.translation: That's right. That's why some conflicts have arisen lately.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 갈등을 해결하려면 지도자가 책임을 더 명확하게 나눠야 해요.
dialogue.translation: To resolve the conflict, the leader should distribute responsibilities more clearly.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 하지만 그는 오히려 모든 것을 통제하려고 해요.
dialogue.translation: But he, on the contrary, tries to control everything.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그러면 팀원들이 더 불만을 갖게 되겠네요.
dialogue.translation: Then the team members will become more dissatisfied.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그래서 저는 그에게 의견을 말했어요. 그가 좀 바뀌기를 바라요.
dialogue.translation: So I told him my opinion. I hope he changes a bit.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 좋은 지도자는 팀의 의견을 듣고, 책임을 공유하면서 갈등을 해결하는 사람이에요.
dialogue.translation: A good leader is someone who listens to the team's opinions, shares responsibilities, and resolves conflicts.
